slides.title: Angular 14+ Revolution 🚀
slides.content:
# Standalone Components

Introduced in Angular 14, **standalone components** are components, directives, or pipes that are *not* declared in any NgModule.

They manage their own dependencies via `standalone: true` and the `imports` array inside the component decorator.

This simplifies Angular architecture – no more module files just to declare components. It’s the future of Angular development.

slides.title: Mixing with NgModules 🔄
slides.content:
Angular allows seamless interoperability:
* You can import an NgModule into a standalone component’s `imports`.
* You can import a standalone component into an NgModule’s `imports` array.

This means you can gradually migrate an existing module‑based app to standalone without a big bang rewrite.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Start New Projects with Standalone

Angular CLI now generates components with `standalone: true` by default (since v17+). Embrace it for simpler, flatter project structures.

quizData.question: Standalone components cannot be used together with NgModules.
quizData.explanation: They can be freely mixed; standalone components can import modules and vice versa.
